newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Coffee seen steadying but still risks fall.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Coffee seen steadying but still risks fall.

text.p: JULY Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
LIFFE coffee is expected to be steadier on Monday after a steep tumble last week, but analysts still saw a risk of a further move down.
July coffee was called to open between $50 and $70 higher to recover some of last week's sharp losses. On Friday, London July robustas lost $80, or 4.2 percent, to end at $1,825 per tonne.
But New York's arabicas had started to recover from the week's sharp slide to end higher on Friday at 237.25 cents per pound, up 6.75 cents.

Cornelia Dichio, analyst at Chart Watch, saw a potentially strong support base nearby, derived from the January to May range, starting at $1,800 for July robustas. The bottom of the support range rests near $1,500.
"There will be some marginal steadying," she said. But after a massive, accelerated drop last week, she did not rule out further downside risk.
She said the market's dynamics near the support base would be key in determining coffee's next move.

After the market closed on Friday, the latest CFTC's commitment of traders report showed 7,203 non-commercial longs and 12,283 non-reportable longs. Both were down from the previous report and should help slow coffee's downside momentum in the near term.
